title: add-rag-authoring-patterns-di-mocks-and-offline-replay-quickstart
author: Sofia Martínez
release_notes: New quickstart: RAG authoring patterns. Adds dependency-injection examples, mock tool providers for deterministic local tests, and an offline replay runner for deterministic E2E replays. No breaking API changes.
description: Context and motivation: Teams keep asking for repeatable RAG authoring workflows that make tool-calling behavior testable and portable between local dev, CI, and Private deployments. This PR introduces a compact quickstart that demonstrates three companion patterns: 1) dependency-injection (DI) for tool bindings so authors can swap real connectors for deterministic mocks; 2) a lightweight mock tool provider package with examples (HTTP adapter, DB read stub, and a scrape/tool wrapper) and telemetry hooks; 3) an offline 'replay-runner' that captures a session's tool calls and model inputs and replays them deterministically for CI/evaluation and regression hunting. Checklist: - [x] Add quickstart scaffold and README with step-by-step usage - [x] Implement DI utilities and examples in TypeScript - [x] Add mock tool provider implementations and tests - [x] Add replay-runner CLI with session capture format and verification hooks - [x] Add devcontainer and CI job for smoke/e2e validation - [x] Update docs site sidebar and quickstart index Files changed summary: - quickstarts/rag-di-mocks/README.md: new quickstart walkthrough and rationale - quickstarts/rag-di-mocks/devcontainer.json: reproducible dev container - quickstarts/rag-di-mocks/src/di.ts: DI helpers (registerBinder, resolveBinder) - quickstarts/rag-di-mocks/src/mocks/*.ts: mock tool providers (httpStub, dbStub, fileTool) - quickstarts/rag-di-mocks/src/replay/replay-runner.ts: capture & replay CLI - quickstarts/rag-di-mocks/tests/*: unit and smoke tests - docs/quickstarts/index.yaml: registration in docs site - ci/workflows/rag-quickstart-e2e.yml: new CI job Commits (high-level): - 11c3a2f initial scaffold and README - 2b9f5d1 add DI helpers and examples - f4e7a9b implement mock HTTP and DB stubs + tests - a1d8c6e add replay-runner CLI and session format - 7e5b0f3 wire up devcontainer and CI job - 0f9d4c2 fix test race and telemetry hook Review conversation summary: - Liam Chen (reviewer): "Love the DI approach. Can we make the binder API smaller? The register/resolve surface looks slightly verbose for tiny playbooks." - Sofia (author): "Ack. I extracted a thin facade (registerBinder/withBindings) and added a short example in README showing the minimal pattern." - Priya Kapoor: "Tests look good but CI failed on the first run due to a flakey file write in replay-runner. Suggest using tmpdir utilities from our test harness." - Sofia: "Fixed in 0f9d4c2, now uses tmpdir and adds retries for a short fs sync window. Added e2e smoke in CI to reduce regressions." - Evan Brooks: "Docs copy should emphasize determinism for replayed sessions and how to pin model versions in Redwood Console for matching outputs." - Sofia: "Updated README and added a small note to docs/quickstarts/index.yaml with cross-links to model pinning docs." CI summary: - First CI run failed (unit test flake in replay-runner file handling) - Patch 0f9d4c2 added tmpdir and removed timing assumptions; re-ran CI - All checks passed (unit, lint, TypeScript build, quick e2e smoke) Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main after approvals from Liam and Priya; merge commit message references ENG-1428 and PM-301. How to use (quick): 1) git clone && cd quickstarts/rag-di-mocks 2) npm ci && npm run devcontainer:open (optional) 3) npm run start to run a local playbook against mock providers 4) npm run capture-session to record tool calls, then npm run replay-session --session <file> to deterministically replay in CI Notes on design decisions: - DI facades were chosen to keep quickstart ergonomics high; heavy DI frameworks were intentionally avoided. - Replay format is JSONL with explicit model input and tool-call records so it can be compressed and archived in evaluations. - Telemetry hooks emit light-weight probes (event:tool_call, event:replay_start) compatible with the quickstart telemetry presets. Backwards compatibility: No changes to Redwood runtime or APIs. This is authoring-side code that uses the existing public SDKs. Related work: docs site quickstart index (PR ENG-1292), telemetry presets work (ENG-1401).
commits: 11c3a2f initial scaffold and README; 2b9f5d1 add DI helpers and examples; f4e7a9b implement mock HTTP and DB stubs + tests; a1d8c6e add replay-runner CLI and session format; 7e5b0f3 wire up devcontainer and CI job; 0f9d4c2 fix test race and telemetry hook
notes_for_maintainers: This quickstart is intentionally self-contained. Ensure the CI job uses a small GPU or CPU-only token since it relies on mock providers; the job is labeled 'quickstart-e2e' and should be low-cost. If telemetry presets change, update quickstarts/rag-di-mocks/telemetry-mapping.md accordingly.
changelog_entry: Added RAG authoring quickstart demonstrating dependency-injection patterns, mock tool providers, and an offline replay-runner for deterministic testing and CI.
testing_instructions: Run npm ci && npm test to execute the unit tests. For end-to-end: npm run capture-session to produce sessions/sample.jsonl then npm run replay-session -- --file sessions/sample.jsonl. CI job rag-quickstart-e2e.yml demonstrates the minimal pipeline.
security_considerations: Mocks are safe for local dev only; quickstart warns about not using mocked secrets in production. Replay files may contain payloads; guidance added to README to redact sensitive fields before archival.
future_work: Follow-up PR to add a Go and Python variant of the DI/mocks pattern (ENG-1502). Consider adding an SDK helper to validate session compatibility with pinned model versions.
human_readable_summary: A small, production-oriented quickstart that helps developers author RAG playbooks with deterministic testing. Patterns included: dependency-injection for tool binding, mock tool providers, and an offline replay-runner for CI and regression debugging. Merged after fixes to a flakey test and a brief review cycle.
